concepts.learning_objective: Explain why lengths measured with body parts such as the handspan or stride differ from person to person.
State that a measured length is expressed in two parts, a number and a unit.
Identify the metre as the SI unit of length and distinguish standard from non-standard units.
Convert lengths between kilometre, metre, centimetre and millimetre.
Choose a suitable scale or tape for measuring a given length.
Describe the correct placement of a scale and the correct position of the eye while reading it.
Measure a length with a scale whose ends are broken by subtracting the starting mark reading.

topics.title: Measuring the Length of a Curved Line

concepts.learning_objective: Measure the length of a curved line using a thread or flexible tape and apply it to find distances.
Write lengths with the correct unit symbols, spacing and lowercase letters.
Define a reference point and identify it in everyday situations.
Interpret how the position of an object changes with respect to a reference point.
Decide whether an object is at rest or in motion from the change in its position with time.
Explain that the same object can be at rest or in motion depending on the chosen reference point.

topics.title: Types of Motion: Linear and Circular Motion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify linear motion as motion along a straight line.
Identify circular motion as motion along a circular path.

topics.title: Types of Motion: Oscillatory and Periodic Motion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify oscillatory motion as to-and-fro motion about a fixed position.
Explain that circular and oscillatory motions are periodic because the path repeats after a fixed interval of time.
